title: Control-room journey gate
description: Objective: prove J1-J6 end to end against a real daemon with accessibility, degraded, cursor-gap, approval, graph, and recovery fixtures. Deliverable: Playwright journey evidence at one exact commit. NOT in scope: portability adapters or GA claims. Hard dependencies: every M3 surface and Graph operator journeys. Owned paths: tests/e2e/control-room/** and release evidence paths only. Verification: pnpm test:e2e.
definitionOfDone: All pinned J1-J6 acceptance criteria and twenty scenario-matrix cases pass.
Truth, provenance, keyboard, narrow-window, loading, degraded, and latency invariants pass globally.
No action exists without an allowed daemon command and no transcript enters clean review.
Playwright gate exits 0 at one exact commit.
taskRails: The standalone control room displays daemon truth and nextAllowedCommands; it never derives authority, readiness, or evidence strength.
Every fact is text/icon/color encoded, keyboard accessible, provenance-drillable, and honest under degraded data.
IDE adapters remain thin optional launch/discover/embed shells with no product logic. Keep modules below 400 lines; explicit owned paths only.

implementationPlan.description:

A frozen list of every J1-J6 acceptance criterion and every one of the twenty scenario-matrix cases, each entry: { id, journey, status: "COVERED" | "UNKNOWN", missingInput?, owner? }.

Rules that keep it from rotting:
  - Every UNKNOWN MUST carry a non-empty missingInput and an owner. An UNKNOWN that does not say what is missing is indistinguishable from a silent pass.
  - The five graph ids are UNKNOWN with owner task-779d6804 and missingInput naming the absent surface. State in a comment that the task is ARCHIVED, so a later reader does not wait on it.
  - Assert the total case count equals twenty (DoD 1's number), and assert COVERED + UNKNOWN sums to that total. A case quietly deleted must fail.
  - Assert the COVERED count is greater than zero — a ledger where everything is UNKNOWN is not a gate.
  - Assert every COVERED id actually resolves to a production file on disk, so a scenario cannot be marked covered for a surface that does not exist. This is the check that would have caught the graph half automatically.

WRITE THE COVERED JOURNEY SPECS — tests/e2e/control-room/journeys.spec.ts, driven through the real browser against the real built bundle via the existing harness.

Compose harness.ts and static-ports.ts; do not reimplement bundle serving or port selection inside the spec. Follow control-room-smoke.spec.ts's existing setup shape.

Cover the J1-J6 criteria whose surfaces exist, and the DoD 2 invariants that are genuinely checkable in a browser:
  TRUTH and PROVENANCE — every displayed fact is text-encoded and provenance-drillable.
  KEYBOARD — every action reachable and operable by keyboard; assert focus actually moves, not merely that a handler exists.
  NARROW WINDOW — resize to the narrow breakpoint and assert action parity rather than mere presence.
  LOADING and DEGRADED — drive the degraded and cursor-gap fixtures and assert the surface stays honest: UNKNOWN renders as UNKNOWN, never as a confident value or a blank.

DoD 3, and it is the strongest claim here: assert NO ACTION EXISTS WITHOUT AN ALLOWED DAEMON COMMAND. Enumerate every rendered cr.action.* in each journey and assert each maps to a nextAllowedCommand. Assert the enumerated count is greater than zero first — a sweep that finds no actions would otherwise pass trivially. Also assert no transcript enters clean review.

A browser test that only asserts an element is present proves the DOM rendered, not that the journey works. Assert observable OUTCOMES of real interactions — what changed after the click, where focus landed, what the surface says now.

implementationPlan.note:
ASSERTIONS ADDED. Node lane now 23 tests, up from the 15 QA ran, and the delta is exactly the 8 I wrote — 1 loading record + 3 rot-guard cases + 4 invariant-ledger. Counted rather than assumed. `npx vitest run tests/e2e/control-room/journey-coverage.test.ts` -> 1 file, 23 passed, 297ms.

1. LOADING RECORD, mirroring the latency assertions at :130-135. Pins status UNKNOWN, cause SURFACE_NOT_COMPOSED, non-empty missingInput and owner. It also asserts missingInput CONTAINS cr.board.skeleton, cr.goals.loading and cr.health.loading. Pinning the CAUSE matters as much as the status: downgrading it to SURFACE_ABSENT would be a plausible-looking edit that silently points the next reader at the wrong owner, since those components genuinely exist.

2. ROT GUARD, and it is WIDER than QA asked for on purpose. QA specified control-room-preview.tsx. main.tsx:40 branches — `live ? <LiveControlRoom .../> : <ControlRoomScaffold />` — so guarding only the preview would let loading become reachable down the ?live=1 path while the ledger still called it UNKNOWN, which is the same rot in a different file. Guards all three served modules: preview/control-room-preview.tsx, live/live-app.tsx, live/live-board.tsx. Each asserts existsSync FIRST, because a guard reading a renamed file asserts over an empty string and passes while proving nothing.

Matcher is `not.toMatch(/\bloading=/u)`, deliberately the same shape as the existing `/\bbreaker=/u` guard. I rejected the stricter `/\bloading\b/u`: a comment mentioning the word would redden it for no real reason, and the claim being guarded is that no served module PASSES the prop, not that the word never appears.

3. THE DoD 2 INVARIANT LEDGER, four tests: exact seven-id list in DoD order; COVERED+UNKNOWN equals seven with COVERED greater than zero and the UNKNOWN set pinned to exactly [LOADING, LATENCY]; every UNKNOWN carrying non-empty cause/missingInput/owner; and the binding below.

4. THE LOAD-BEARING ONE — every COVERED invariant's `provenBy` titles must resolve to real `test("...")` declarations in journeys.spec.ts. This is what makes the ledger non-decorative: delete the keyboard test and the ledger goes RED rather than continuing to claim the invariant holds, which is exactly what did NOT happen for loading. It asserts `(SPEC.match(/^test\(/gmu) ?? []).length` is greater than zero BEFORE the sweep, so a spec file that failed to read or changed declaration style cannot make every `includes` pass over nothing — the zero-case failure mode epic rail 6 names.

Matched as the literal substring `test("<title>"` rather than a built regex, so a title containing regex metacharacters cannot silently fail to match.

I did NOT re-assert the five covered invariants' browser behaviour here. journeys.spec.ts already asserts it and re-checking it in the Node lane would be a helper reimplementing the production surface — the thing epic rail 6 forbids. This block asserts the LEDGER is honest about what that file proves; that file proves the behaviour.

implementationPlan.description:
MUTATION DRILLS — prove each guard is reddenable. Run each, confirm the NAMED assertion kills it, revert, confirm green before the next.

  2. Delete one scenario entry -> the total-equals-twenty assertion must go RED.
  3. Blank an UNKNOWN's missingInput -> the non-empty assertion must go RED.
  4. Flip latency from UNKNOWN to COVERED -> its status assertion must go RED.
  5. Remove a nextAllowedCommand binding from a rendered action -> the DoD 3 action/command assertion must go RED. If it stays green, that assertion is enumerating zero actions and the non-zero precondition is missing.
  6. Strip the keyboard handler from one action -> the keyboard invariant must go RED, proving it asserts focus movement rather than element presence.

SHARED-WORKTREE HAZARD: a foreign completion hook can whole-tree commit your mutation while it is on disk — that happened to a file of mine earlier in this session. After each revert check BOTH `git diff -- <file>` AND `git status --porcelain <file>`; a clean diff alone is not proof.
implementationPlan.note:
SIX DRILLS ON THE NEW GUARDS. Each reddened at the assertion I aimed at, each restored, green re-confirmed between. Two of them were BAD DRILLS first and I redid them; both failures are recorded below because each taught something.

1. FLIP LOADING_RECORD TO COVERED (QA's named drill).
   RED: "AssertionError: expected 'COVERED' to be 'UNKNOWN'", 1 failed | 22 passed.
   *** THIS DRILL FOUND A REAL DEFECT IN MY OWN DESIGN. *** Only ONE test reddened. The invariant ledger's UNKNOWN-set assertion stayed GREEN, because journey-invariants.ts hand-wrote `status: "UNKNOWN"` for its LOADING entry while deriving cause/missingInput/owner. Two sources of truth for one fact — precisely the drift that module's doc comment claims to avoid, sitting inside the artifact whose whole purpose is not to lie. Fixed by deriving `status: LOADING_RECORD.status` (and the same for LATENCY).
   RE-DRILLED AFTER THE FIX and the flip is now UNREPRESENTABLE, not merely detected: tsc exits 1 with "Type ... is missing the following properties from type 'CoveredInvariant': bar, provenBy". Marking loading covered now requires naming a bar and the tests that prove it, which is exactly the work that would make it true. A compile error is a stronger guard than a red test.

2. ROT GUARD AGAINST REAL PRODUCTION BYTES. Added `loading={false}` to <ActiveWorkspace> in control-room-preview.tsx.
   RED: "expected 'import { useState } from \"react\";\nim…' not to match /\bloading=/u", 1 failed | 22 passed. Proves the guard reads that file's real contents, not a cached or empty string.
   RESTORED and verified THREE ways, because a clean `git status` alone is not proof here: `grep -c 'loading=' <file>` -> 0, `git status --porcelain <file>` empty, `git diff --stat` empty.

3. RENAME A PROVING TEST in journeys.spec.ts ("...gets focus back" -> "...gets focus BACK").
   RED: "PROVENANCE -> a focused truth chip drills to provenance by keyboard and gets focus back: expected false to be true". The label names both the invariant and the missing title. This is the drill that matters most: it proves the ledger cannot keep claiming an invariant is COVERED after the test proving it is renamed or deleted — the failure mode that let loading go unrecorded in the first place.

4. BLANK LOADING_RECORD.missingInput.
   FIRST ATTEMPT WAS A BAD DRILL AND PASSED 23/23. I deleted only the first sentence, leaving a string that was still non-empty and still contained the three ids — so every assertion legitimately held. The guard was fine; my mutation was too weak. A 23/23 here would have read as "the guard is decorative" if I had not looked at what I actually changed.
   REDONE with `missingInput: ""` -> 2 failed | 21 passed: "expected '' not to be ''" on the record, and "LOADING missingInput: expected '' not to be ''" on the invariant ledger. The second failure also confirms the derivation from drill 1 is live.

5. SUBSTITUTE THE LOADING ENTRY (id "LOADING" -> "LATENCY", so the list still has seven members).
   RED on two: "expected [ 'TRUTH', 'PROVENANCE', …(5) ] to deeply equal [...]" and "expected [ 'LATENCY', 'LATENCY' ] to deeply equal [ 'LOADING', 'LATENCY' ]".
   WORTH KNOWING: THE COUNT STAYED SEVEN. A `toHaveLength(7)` assertion alone would have passed this substitution silently. The whole-list compare is the load-bearing guard, not the count — the same lesson QA's drill 5 taught about the on-disk file check.
   (My first attempt at this one was also bad: I replaced a closing token with invalid syntax inside a batch script whose `set -e` did not stop it, so the result was unreadable. Redone as a clean single-token substitution.)

6. EMPTY A provenBy ARRAY (NARROW_WINDOW).
   RED: "NARROW_WINDOW provenBy: expected 0 to be greater than 0". Proves the non-vacuity precondition works — an empty provenBy cannot let the title sweep pass over zero cases, which is the epic rail 6 defect.
